## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(easystats)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(patchwork)
library(ggside)
library(ggdist)

# Everything that needs a fitted model -- the units, the prediction grid, and
# the predictions themselves -- is in server/predictions.R, shared with the
# cluster job that runs it (`./hpc predict <model>`, then `./hpc pull
# predictions`). This script only reads its results, relabels them and plots,
# so it never has to hold the fits in memory.
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/predictions.R" else "analysis/server/predictions.R")
```


```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

# path <- "C:/Users/olive/Documents/"
path <- if (dir.exists("models")) "models/" else "analysis/models/"

pred_path <- paste0(path, "predictions/")

# The same models fitted in stanli instead of cmdstanr, the sampler tests of
# server/AGENT.md 6.6-6.8. They have the production names, so they have a
# directory of their own, laid out the same way (`IGC_BACKEND=stanli ./hpc pull
# predictions` fills its predictions/).
stanli_path <- sub("models/$", "models_stanli/", path)
model_dirs <- c(cmdstanr = path, stanli = stanli_path)

# A fit does not know which illusion it was fitted to: its data only has the
# Z-scored predictors, and combine_model.R drops $file. The file name is the one
# place it is recorded (<model>_<illusion>[_suffix].rds), so it is attached to
# the fit here, for model_illusion(). Only needed to compute predictions
# locally (see load_predictions() below).
load_fit <- function(file, dir = path) {
  illusion <- regmatches(file, regexpr("MullerLyer|Ebbinghaus|VerticalHorizontal", file))
  if (length(illusion) == 0) stop("No illusion in the file name: ", file)
  m <- readRDS(paste0(dir, file))
  attr(m, "illusion") <- illusion
  m
}

# The results of server/predictions.R for one model, from
# models/predictions/<name>.rds as written by `./hpc predict` and fetched by
# `./hpc pull predictions` (models_stanli/ for the stanli fit). A model with no
# such file but a fit in models/ has them computed here instead, once, and
# saved to the same place -- slow, and it loads the fit, but it means a fit
# pulled without its predictions still works. Delete a prediction file to have
# it recomputed. The sampler is recorded in $meta$sampler, which the files
# themselves do not have.
load_predictions <- function(name, sampler = "cmdstanr") {
  dir <- model_dirs[[sampler]]
  hpc <- if (sampler == "stanli") "IGC_BACKEND=stanli ./hpc" else "./hpc"
  file <- paste0(dir, "predictions/", name, ".rds")
  fit_file <- paste0(dir, name, ".rds")
  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
      stop("No predictions and no fit for ", name, " (", sampler, "): run `", hpc, " predict ",
           sub("_[^_]+$", "", name), "` and `", hpc, " pull predictions`.")
    }
    message("No predictions for ", name, " (", sampler, "): computing them from the local fit (slow).")
    fit <- load_fit(basename(fit_file), dir)
    rez <- run_predictions(fit, name, fit_file = fit_file)
    rm(fit)
    gc()
    dir.create(paste0(dir, "predictions/"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    saveRDS(rez, file)
  }
  rez <- readRDS(file)

  if (!identical(rez$meta$version, igc_predictions_version)) {
    stop(name, " (", sampler, "): the predictions are format ", rez$meta$version,
         " and this script reads ", igc_predictions_version, ". Re-run `", hpc,
         " predict`, or delete ", file, " to recompute locally.")
  }
  # A fit re-combined or re-fitted since. The size is compared rather than the
  # time, which a copy does not always keep.
  if (file.exists(fit_file) && !identical(file.size(fit_file), rez$meta$fit_size)) {
    warning(name, ": the predictions were made from another fit than ", fit_file,
            ". Re-run `", hpc, " predict`, or delete ", file, " to recompute locally.")
  }
  # Every curve and heatmap is drawn over the reliable predictor space
  # (plot_ranges in server/predictions.R), whatever range the file was made
  # over: a wider one is cropped to it. A file that does not cover it all (the
  # Müller-Lyer files made before 2026-11-25 start at a difference of 0.05,
  # not 0.045) is drawn over what it has.
  if (!covers_plot_range(rez$meta$plot_range, rez$meta$illusion)) {
    message(name, " (", sampler, "): the predictions do not cover all of plot_ranges. Re-run `",
            hpc, " predict` for the whole reliable space.")
  }
  rez$curves <- crop_to_plot_range(rez$curves, rez$meta$illusion)
  rez$heatmaps <- crop_to_plot_range(rez$heatmaps, rez$meta$illusion)
  rez$meta$sampler <- sampler
  rez
}

# The models to compare, per illusion, by file name, in the order they should
# appear in the plots below. Every section has one tab per illusion, and
# everything in a tab loops over that illusion's list, so adding a model here is
# the only change needed to get it into the predictive check, the curves and the
# heatmaps. Adding an illusion takes an entry here and a tab in each section.
models <- list(
  MullerLyer = c(
    "LNR" = "gam_lnr_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",
    "LNR-6" = "gam_lnr6_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",  # NOT CONVERGED: sigmabias modes, 4:4 on the 2026-10-13 refit (asf25, uploaded 2026-11-16; server/AGENT.md 4.10 B)
    "DDM-4" = "gam_ddm4_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",
    "DDM-5" = "gam_ddm5_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",  # converged (cc831, uploaded 2026-11-16)
    "RDM" = "gam_rdm_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",  # converged, cmdstanr refit 11698239 (combined 2026-11-23; its stanli twin agrees, ELPD diff 0.2)
    "RDM-5" = "gam_rdm5_mullerlyer_MullerLyer",  # NOT CONVERGED: sigmabias modes, 6:2 again on the 2026-10-13 refit (server/AGENT.md 4.10 B)
    "LBA" = "gam_lba_mullerlyer_MullerLyer"  # NOT CONVERGED: the 2026-10-13 refit (oc236, delivered 2026-11-17) split 6:2, like the two before (server/AGENT.md 4.9, 4.10 B)
  ),
  VerticalHorizontal = c(
    "LNR" = "gam_lnr_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",
    "LNR-6" = "gam_lnr6_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",  # converged on the 2026-10-13 refit (asf25)
    "DDM-4" = "gam_ddm4_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",
    "DDM-5" = "gam_ddm5_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",  # converged, cmdstanr refit 11698241 (combined 2026-11-23; its stanli twin agrees, ELPD diff 0.9)
    "RDM" = "gam_rdm_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",  # converged, cmdstanr refit 11698240 (combined 2026-11-25; its stanli twin agrees, ELPD diff 1.3)
    "RDM-5" = "gam_rdm5_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal",  # NOT CONVERGED: sigmabias modes, 6:2 on the 2026-10-13 refit (server/AGENT.md 4.10 B)
    "LBA" = "gam_lba_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal"  # NOT CONVERGED: four clusters on the 2026-10-13 refit (oc236, delivered 2026-11-17; server/AGENT.md 4.10 B)
  ),
  Ebbinghaus = c(
    # NOT CONVERGED, and worse than the others: warmup never reached the posterior.
    # The cogmod 0.3.5 refit with 1500 warmup (11626373 on cc831, combined

    "LNR" = "gam_lnr_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus",
    "LNR-6" = "gam_lnr6_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus",  # 1 of 4 shards on the 2026-10-13 refit, with the gam_lnr_ebbinghaus adaptation failure (server/AGENT.md 4.10 C); refitting in stanli as 11819833 (2026-11-24, 6.13), which will be picked up from models_stanli/ once predicted
    "DDM-4" = "gam_ddm4_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus",

    "RDM" = "gam_rdm_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus",  # stanli stand-in until the cmdstanr refit 11698242

    "LBA" = "gam_lba_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus"  # NOT CONVERGED: 6:2 split on the 2026-10-13 refit (oc236, delivered 2026-11-17; server/AGENT.md 4.10 B)

# Which fit each model's results come from. A model is its cmdstanr fit, the
# production one. Its stanli fit, the same model sampled by another sampler,
# stands in only while there is no cmdstanr fit (still running on the cluster,
# or too slow to finish), and is otherwise used only in the sampler comparison
# below. A model with neither is left out of its tab rather than stopping the
# whole render.
has_results <- function(name, sampler) {
  dir <- model_dirs[[sampler]]
  file.exists(paste0(dir, "predictions/", name, ".rds")) | file.exists(paste0(dir, name, ".rds"))
}

# Every model that has a stanli fit, whether or not its cmdstanr twin is there
# yet, for the sampler comparison
twins <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, illusion) {
  data.frame(Illusion = illusion, Model = names(m), Name = unname(m))
}) |>
  mutate(cmdstanr = has_results(Name, "cmdstanr"), stanli = has_results(Name, "stanli")) |>
  filter(stanli)

samplers <- lapply(models, \(m) {
  setNames(ifelse(has_results(m, "cmdstanr"), "cmdstanr",
                  ifelse(has_results(m, "stanli"), "stanli", NA_character_)),
           names(m))
})
skipped <- unlist(Map(\(m, s) m[is.na(s)], models, samplers))
if (length(skipped) > 0) message("Not available yet, skipped: ", paste(skipped, collapse = ", "))
standins <- unlist(Map(\(m, s) m[s %in% "stanli"], models, samplers))
if (length(standins) > 0) {
  message("No cmdstanr fit yet, its stanli fit stands in: ", paste(standins, collapse = ", "))
}
# The same, for the table under "Fits Used"
model_status <- purrr::imap_dfr(samplers, \(s, illusion) {
  data.frame(Illusion = illusion, Model = names(s), Source = unname(s))
})
models <- Map(\(m, s) m[!is.na(s)], models, samplers)
samplers <- lapply(samplers, \(s) s[!is.na(s)])
preds <- Map(\(m, s) Map(load_predictions, m, s), models, samplers)

# One colour per model, whatever the illusion, so a model looks the same in
# every tab. A hue per family of models, and within a family the variant with
# more parameters is the darker one (DDM: orange to dark red, LNR: blue, RDM:
# green). 1_models.qmd has the same colours.
model_colors <- c("LNR" = "#1E88E5", "LNR-6" = "#0D47A1", "DDM-4" = "#FB8C00", "DDM-5" = "#B71C1C",
                  "RDM" = "#43A047", "RDM-5" = "#1B5E20", "LBA" = "#8E24AA")

# For the tables: the same colours behind the model names, and a way to fill
# the cells of a column. The text is white on a dark fill and black on a light
# one.
text_on <- function(fill) {
  lum <- apply(grDevices::col2rgb(fill), 2, \(x) sum(c(0.299, 0.587, 0.114) * x)) / 255
  ifelse(lum < 0.55, "white", "black")
}
fill_cells <- function(tab, j, fill) {
  for (i in seq_along(fill)) {
    tab <- tinytable::style_tt(tab, i = i, j = j, background = fill[i], color = text_on(fill[i]))
  }
  tab
}
model_fill <- function(labels) {
  fill <- model_colors[as.character(labels)]
  fill[is.na(fill)] <- "#BDBDBD"
  unname(fill)
}
```

## Fits Used

Every production fit is cmdstanr. A model that so far has only a stanli fit
uses that fit as a stand-in until its cmdstanr refit is combined (the two
samplers agree, see the appendix). "not yet": in the list, but no results on
this machine. "—": not in that illusion's list (see the comments in `models`
above).

```{r}
status <- model_status |>
  mutate(Source = case_when(Source == "cmdstanr" ~ "cmdstanr",
                            Source == "stanli" ~ "stanli (stand-in)",
                            .default = "not yet"),
         Illusion = c(MullerLyer = "Muller-Lyer", VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal",
                      Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus")[Illusion]) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion, values_from = Source, values_fill = "—")

source_fill <- c("cmdstanr" = "#C8E6C9", "stanli (stand-in)" = "#FFE082",
                 "not yet" = "#EEEEEE", "—" = "#FFFFFF")
out <- tinytable::tt(status) |>
  fill_cells(1, model_fill(status$Model))
for (j in 2:ncol(status)) out <- fill_cells(out, j, unname(source_fill[status[[j]]]))
out
```

## Convergence

A model is only worth comparing if its chains agree. "Population" is the
smooth coefficients, their SDs and the group-level SDs. The participant
offsets count only in the "all" columns, where a few participants above 1.01
do not sink an otherwise sound fit. The verdict is the worst of the coloured
cells. An acceptable fit can be interpreted at the population level. The ones
here all have their 8 chains in one mode. They miss the strictest cut-offs by
about what the maximum over some 40 parameters gives by chance, or by a
handful of divergent draws out of 8,000. The fits that did not converge miss
by far more, with R-hat around 1.5 or above.

| | satisfactory | acceptable | poor |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-hat (population, and lp__) | ≤ 1.01 | ≤ 1.05 (lp__: ≤ 1.1) | above |
| Bulk ESS (population, minimum) | ≥ 400 | ≥ 100 | below |
| Divergent transitions | none | under 1% | 1% or more |

```{r}
# What compute_convergence() in server/predictions.R stored for each model. A
# prediction file made before it existed has none, and is listed as not computed.
show_convergence <- function(preds) {
  conv <- lapply(preds, \(p) p$convergence)
  have <- !vapply(conv, is.null, logical(1))
  if (any(!have)) {
    cat("Not computed yet (re-run `./hpc predict` and pull): ",
        paste(names(preds)[!have], collapse = ", "), "
", sep = "")
  }
  if (!any(have)) return(invisible(NULL))
  conv <- conv[have]
  sampler <- vapply(preds[have], \(p) p$meta$sampler, character(1))
  get <- \(k) vapply(conv, \(x) as.numeric(x[[k]]), numeric(1))

  rhat_pop <- get("rhat_pop_max")
  rhat_all <- get("rhat_all_max")
  rhat_lp <- get("rhat_lp")
  ess <- get("ess_bulk_pop_min")
  div <- get("divergent")
  div_pct <- get("divergent_pct")

  # 1 = satisfactory, 2 = acceptable, 3 = poor. A missing value (the sampler
  # diagnostics could not be read) is not counted against the model.
  grade <- \(x, ok, warn, higher_is_worse = TRUE) {
    if (!higher_is_worse) { x <- -x; ok <- -ok; warn <- -warn }
    ifelse(is.na(x), 1L, ifelse(x <= ok, 1L, ifelse(x <= warn, 2L, 3L)))
  }
  g_rhat <- grade(rhat_pop, 1.01, 1.05)
  g_lp <- grade(rhat_lp, 1.01, 1.1)
  g_ess <- grade(ess, 400, 100, higher_is_worse = FALSE)
  g_div <- ifelse(is.na(div), 1L, ifelse(div == 0, 1L, ifelse(div_pct < 1, 2L, 3L)))
  g_all <- pmax(g_rhat, g_lp, g_ess, g_div)

  palette <- c("#C8E6C9", "#FFE082", "#EF9A9A")
  verdict <- c("Satisfactory", "Acceptable", "Poor")

  n_params <- get("n_params")
  tab <- data.frame(
    Model = names(conv),
    Sampler = ifelse(sampler == "stanli", "stanli (stand-in)", sampler),
    Chains = get("n_chains"),
    "R-hat, population (max)" = formatC(rhat_pop, format = "f", digits = 3),
    "R-hat, all (max)" = formatC(rhat_all, format = "f", digits = 3),
    "All parameters above 1.01" = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * get("n_rhat_101_all") / n_params),
    "R-hat, lp__" = formatC(rhat_lp, format = "f", digits = 3),
    "Bulk ESS, population (min)" = formatC(ess, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","),
    "Divergent" = ifelse(is.na(div), "n/a", sprintf("%d (%.2f%%)", as.integer(div), div_pct)),
    "At max treedepth" = ifelse(is.na(get("treedepth_hit_pct")), "n/a",
                                sprintf("%.0f%%", get("treedepth_hit_pct"))),
    Verdict = verdict[g_all],
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  out <- tinytable::tt(tab) |>
    tinytable::style_tt(j = 3:10, align = "r") |>
    fill_cells(1, model_fill(tab$Model)) |>
    fill_cells(4, palette[g_rhat]) |>
    fill_cells(7, palette[g_lp]) |>
    fill_cells(8, palette[g_ess]) |>
    fill_cells(9, palette[g_div]) |>
    fill_cells(11, palette[g_all])
  out
}
```

### Participants That Do Not Mix

Even in the models that converge, a few dozen participants do not mix. Their
own parameters sit in one of two local solutions, and no chain switches
between them. Almost always it is the non-decision time traded against the
boundary or the outlier probability (`server/AGENT.md` 4.10). None is
excluded: no rule on the data picks them out without also removing many
participants who mix well. The list comes from `server/mixing_participants.R`.

::: {.callout-warning}
This list comes from the fits before the 2026-10-13 refit (its model names
are the old `gam_<family>`). It is out of date until `mixing_participants.R`
is re-run on the refit's combined fits.
:::

```{r}
mixing <- read.csv(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/poorly_mixing_participants.csv"
                   else "analysis/server/poorly_mixing_participants.csv")
data_dir <- if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data" else "data"
illu <- bind_rows(lapply(1:3, \(i) read.csv(file.path(data_dir, paste0("illusion_part", i, ".csv"))))) |>
  filter(Illusion_Type %in% unique(mixing$Illusion)) |>
  left_join(distinct(mixing, Participant, Illusion_Type = Illusion, Flagged = TRUE),
            by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type")) |>
  mutate(Flagged = !is.na(Flagged),
         Response = ifelse(Error == 1, "Error", "Correct"))
```

#### Participants

```{r}
mixing |>
  summarize(Models = n(),
            Fits = paste0(Model, " (", Illusion, ")", collapse = ", "),
            Rhat = max(Rhat),
            Parameters = paste(unique(unlist(strsplit(Parameters, ";"))), collapse = ", "),
            .by = c("Participant", "Dataset")) |>
  arrange(desc(Models), desc(Rhat)) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "Rhat", decimals = 2) |>
  gt::opt_interactive(use_search = TRUE, page_size_default = 10)
```

#### Profile

Compared with everyone else who did the same illusion, they respond faster
and more consistently and make more errors, and their errors are no slower
than their correct responses. Each row gives where the median flagged
participant falls among the others (percentile).

```{r}
mixing_profile <- illu |>
  summarize(`Error rate` = mean(Error),
            `Median RT` = median(RT),
            `RT spread (IQR)` = IQR(RT),
            `5th percentile RT` = quantile(RT, 0.05),
            `Errors slower than correct (log RT)` =
              median(log(RT[Error == 1])) - median(log(RT[Error == 0])),
            .by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Flagged"))

mixing_profile |>
  pivot_longer(-c(Participant, Illusion_Type, Flagged), names_to = "Feature") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  summarize(Others = median(value[!Flagged]),
            `Do not mix` = median(value[Flagged]),
            Percentile = 100 * mean(value[!Flagged] < median(value[Flagged])),
            .by = "Feature") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("Others", "Do not mix"), n_sigfig = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "Percentile", decimals = 0)
```

```{r}
# Each of them as a density line, against the pooled RTs of everyone else

illu |>

  ggplot(aes(x = RT)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 0.02, fill = "grey75") +
  geom_density(data = filter(illu, Flagged), aes(group = Participant),
               color = scales::alpha("#E91E63", 0.4), linewidth = 0.4, bounds = c(0, Inf)) +
  scale_x_sqrt(breaks = c(0.15, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 3)) +
  facet_grid(Illusion_Type ~ Response, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(y = NULL, title = "Participants that do not mix (pink) against everyone else (grey)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Computational Cost

```{r}
# Sampling efficiency: bulk ESS per hour of sampling, chain by chain (see
# compute_efficiency() in server/predictions.R for what is counted)
tidy_efficiency <- function(preds) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(preds, \(p, name) mutate(p$efficiency, Model = name, Sampler = p$meta$sampler)) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(preds)))
}

plot_efficiency <- function(preds) {
  efficiency <- tidy_efficiency(preds)

  # Model-level summary: the chains of a model average to one point
  efficiency_means <- efficiency |>
    summarise(.by = Model,
              ESS_per_hour = mean(ESS_per_hour),
              Time_total = mean(Time_total))

  # What each fit was: two models are only comparable here if these match. A
  # stanli stand-in is a different sampler as well (see the appendix).
  caption <- efficiency |>
    summarise(.by = Model,
              label = sprintf("%s: %d chains, %g threads/chain, n = %s%s",
                              first(Model), n(), first(Threads),
                              format(first(N), big.mark = ","),
                              if (first(Sampler) == "stanli") ", stanli (stand-in)" else "")) |>
    pull(label) |>
    paste(collapse = "\n")

  efficiency |>
    ggplot(aes(x = ESS_per_hour, y = Time_total / 3600, colour = Model)) +
    # One point per chain, and the model's mean on top of them
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_point(data = efficiency_means, size = 5, shape = 18) +
    # Both axes log: families differ in cost per gradient by orders of magnitude
    # (the DDM's numerical quadrature is 55x, see server/AGENT.md 4.7.1), and
    # on a linear axis the cheap ones collapse onto the origin
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors) +
    labs(
      x = "Effective sample size per hour of sampling (bulk ESS / h, log)",
      y = "Wall clock per chain, warmup included (hours, log)",
      title = "Computational cost",
      subtitle = "One point per chain, diamond is the model's mean. Bottom right is cheap and efficient.",
      caption = caption
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey40"))
}

# Total compute, three ways, for a rough headline number:
# - Wall clock: the shards of a model run at the same time on the cluster, so
#   what one waited for is the longest chain (queueing, compilation and the
#   combine/loo step are not included).
# - Chains one after the other: the sum of the chain times, i.e. the same run
#   with no parallel chains but still multithreaded within each chain.
# - Single core: that sum times the threads per chain. This assumes within-
#   chain threading scales linearly, which is close to what was measured
#   (4 -> 8 threads halved the time per chain, server/AGENT.md 4.4.1), so read
#   it as an order of magnitude, not a measurement.
table_compute_time <- function(preds) {
  tidy_efficiency(preds) |>
    summarise(.by = Model,
              Chains = n(),
              Threads = first(Threads),
              Cores = n() * first(Threads),
              Wall = max(Time_total) / 3600,
              Serial = sum(Time_total) / 3600,
              SingleCore = sum(Time_total * Threads) / 3600) |>
    mutate(SingleCore_days = SingleCore / 24,
           SingleCore_years = SingleCore / (24 * 365.25)) |>
    gt::gt(rowname_col = "Model") |>
    gt::cols_label(
      Chains = "Chains",
      Threads = "Threads / chain",
      Cores = "Cores used",
      Wall = "Wall clock (h)",
      Serial = "Chains in sequence (h)",
      SingleCore = "Single core (h)",
      SingleCore_days = "Single core (days)",
      SingleCore_years = "Single core (years)"
    ) |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = c(Wall, Serial, SingleCore, SingleCore_days), decimals = 0) |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = SingleCore_years, decimals = 2) |>
    gt::tab_spanner(label = "Without parallelisation (estimated)",
                    columns = c(Serial, SingleCore, SingleCore_days, SingleCore_years)) |>
    gt::tab_source_note("Warmup + sampling only. Single core assumes linear scaling of within-chain threading.")
}
```

## Performance

```{r}
# loo was added at combine time and lives in the fit's $criteria$loo, which the
# prediction files carry over. The list names become the model labels.
# loo_compare() needs two models at least, which an illusion only just started
# on does not have yet.
show_loo <- function(preds) {
  if (length(preds) < 2) {
    cat("Only one model so far (", names(preds), "): nothing to compare.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  rez_loo <- loo_compare(lapply(preds, \(p) p$loo))
  print(report(rez_loo))

  # Ranked by ELPD, best first, as loo_compare() has them. LOOIC is left out: it
  # is -2 x ELPD, so it ranks the models the same way but in the opposite
  # direction (lower is better), which only confuses the table. The model names
  # carry their colour from the plots, and the ELPD cells are shaded from the
  # worst model to the best, so the gaps can be read off the colour. The
  # difference is given with its SE, and the best model, which has none, with a
  # dash. p is the z-test of the difference to the best model.
  tab <- as.data.frame(parameters(rez_loo))
  num <- \(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
  best <- seq_len(nrow(tab)) == 1
  weight <- if (diff(range(tab$ELPD)) == 0) 1 else (tab$ELPD - min(tab$ELPD)) / diff(range(tab$ELPD))
  elpd_fill <- rgb(colorRamp(c("#f7fcf5", "#238b45"))(weight), maxColorValue = 255)

  # Formatted by hand (one decimal, thousands marks): format_tt()'s digits are
  # significant digits, which writes 0 and -176 next to -2,372.7
  tab <- data.frame(
    Model = tab$Name,
    ELPD = num(tab$ELPD),
    "ELPD diff ± SE" = ifelse(best, "—", paste0(num(tab$Difference), " ± ", num(tab$Difference_SE))),
    p = ifelse(is.na(tab$p), "", insight::format_p(tab$p, name = NULL)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  out <- tinytable::tt(tab) |>
    tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:4, align = "r") |>
    fill_cells(1, model_fill(tab$Model)) |>
    fill_cells(2, elpd_fill) |>
    tinytable::style_tt(i = 1, j = 2, bold = TRUE)
  out
}

# What the fit costs against how well it does: the elpd against the time a chain
# took, the y axis of the computational cost plot. The elpd is relative to the
# best model (loo_compare), with the SE of that difference: each model's own SE
# (~800 here) is mostly shared between models fitted to the same trials, and
# would swamp differences that are in fact well resolved.
plot_loo_cost <- function(preds) {
  if (length(preds) < 2) {
    cat("Only one model so far (", names(preds), "): nothing to compare.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  # loo 2.10 returns a data frame with the names in a `model` column, earlier
  # versions a matrix with them as row names
  rez_loo <- as.data.frame(loo_compare(lapply(preds, \(p) p$loo)))
  elpd <- data.frame(
    Model = factor(if (is.null(rez_loo$model)) rownames(rez_loo) else rez_loo$model,
                   levels = names(preds)),
    elpd_diff = rez_loo$elpd_diff,
    se_diff = rez_loo$se_diff
  )

  # One point per chain, as in the cost plot: a model has one elpd, so its
  # chains spread along x only
  efficiency <- tidy_efficiency(preds) |>
    mutate(Time_total = Time_total / 3600) |>
    left_join(elpd, by = "Model")
  efficiency_means <- efficiency |>
    summarise(.by = c(Model, elpd_diff, se_diff),
              Time_total = mean(Time_total))

  ggplot(efficiency, aes(x = Time_total, y = elpd_diff, colour = Model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_linerange(data = efficiency_means,
                   aes(ymin = elpd_diff - se_diff, ymax = elpd_diff + se_diff)) +
    geom_point(data = efficiency_means, size = 5, shape = 18) +
    # Labelled in place: with the colours already shared with every other
    # plot, a legend would only be a lookup. The chains come along with an
    # empty label, which ggrepel then keeps the labels off.
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = bind_rows(mutate(efficiency, Label = ""),
                                              mutate(efficiency_means, Label = as.character(Model))),
                             aes(label = Label),
                             size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", seed = 3, box.padding = 0.5,
                             max.overlaps = Inf) +
    # Log, as in the cost plot
    scale_x_log10() +
    # Headroom above the best model, whose label otherwise has nowhere to go
    # but onto the chains of its neighbours on the zero line
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors, guide = "none") +
    labs(
      x = "Wall clock per chain, warmup included (hours, log)",
      y = "ELPD difference from the best model",
      title = "Performance against computational cost",
      subtitle = paste("Higher is better (dashed: the best model), left is cheaper. Diamond is the model's",
                       "mean over its chains, faint points the chains, bars ±1 SE of the difference.",
                       sep = "\n")
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## Posterior Predictive Check


```{r}
# All models are checked against the same trials: the observed data is taken
# from the first model's file, so the models must share an illusion. What is
# predicted, and how, is compute_ppc() in server/predictions.R.
plot_ppc <- function(preds, rt_range = c(0, 2.5), binwidth = 0.02, n_points = 512, linewidth = 0.9) {

  if (is.null(names(preds))) names(preds) <- paste("Model", seq_along(preds))
  if (length(unique(vapply(preds, \(p) p$meta$illusion, character(1)))) > 1) {
    stop("plot_ppc() compares models fitted to the same illusion.")
  }

  # Observed: histogram of every trial, put on the same defective-density
  # scale. Stored as the count of each distinct (RT, Error), so this is exact.
  observed <- preds[[1]]$ppc$observed
  obs_data <- observed |>
    mutate(bin = floor(RT / binwidth)) |>
    count(Error, bin, wt = n, name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      x = (bin + 0.5) * binwidth,
      y = n / (sum(observed$n) * binwidth) * if_else(Error == 0, 1, -1),
      Response = factor(Error, levels = c(0, 1))
    ) |>
    filter(x <= max(rt_range))

  # Predicted: defective densities, each response's curve scaled by its own
  # rate, so the two areas sum to 1 and correct/error are directly comparable
  # across models. The predicted RTs come binned (1 ms) with the bandwidth
  # density() picked on the raw values, so this is the curve the raw RTs give,
  # to within a bin: density() itself bins its input far more coarsely.
  defective_density <- function(pp) {
    total <- sum(pp$n)
    purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1), function(r) {
      r_chr <- as.character(r)
      if (pp$n[[r_chr]] < 2) return(NULL)
      d <- pp$counts[pp$counts$Response == r, ]
      dens <- density((d$Bin + 0.5) * pp$bin, weights = d$n / sum(d$n), bw = pp$bw[[r_chr]],
                      from = rt_range[1], to = rt_range[2], n = n_points)
      data.frame(
        Response = factor(r, levels = c(0, 1)),
        x = dens$x,
        y = dens$y * (pp$n[[r_chr]] / total) * if (r == 0) 1 else -1
      )
    })
  }
  pred_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(preds, \(p, nm) mutate(defective_density(p$ppc$predicted), Model = nm))
  pred_data$Model <- factor(pred_data$Model, levels = names(preds))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col(
      data = obs_data,
      aes(fill = Response),
      width = binwidth, alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_data,
      aes(color = Model, group = interaction(Model, Response)),
      linewidth = linewidth, alpha = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("0" = "#43A047", "1" = "#F44336"),
      labels = c("0" = "Correct", "1" = "Error")
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = model_colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rt_range) +
    labs(x = "RT", y = "Density", fill = "Observed", color = "Predicted") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.6))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## Parameter Curves

### Process Predictions

```{r}
# Display names for the parameters, in the order they are plotted. Names are
# the family's own ("mu", "ndt", ...), values are what goes in the panel
# titles. Several parameters mean different things from one family to the next
# - "mu" is a drift rate in the DDM and the log-mean of the correct response in
# the LNR, and "sigmabias" is the variability of the starting point in the DDM
# but its maximum (A) in the racing models - so the map is built per family
# (the brms family name, e.g. "cogmod_ddm", as stored in the prediction files).
param_labels <- function(family) {
  lvls <- c("Error Rate" = "Error Rate",
            "Mean RT" = "Mean RT",
            "Median RT" = "Median RT",
            "mu" = "mu",
            "nuone" = "Nu (Errors)",
            "driftone" = "Drift (Errors)",
            "sigmadrift" = "Drift Variability",
            "sigmazero" = "Sigma (Correct)",
            "sigmaone" = "Sigma (Errors)",
            "boundary" = "Boundary",
            "bias" = "Bias",
            "sigmabias" = "Bias Variability",
            "ndt" = "NDT",
            "sigmandt" = "NDT Variability")
  switch(
    family,
    "cogmod_ddm" = {
      lvls["mu"] <- "Drift"
    },
    # sigmabias is only estimated in LNR-6, where it is the start-point range
    # of the race, as in the other racing families. Each accumulator's
    # parameters are kept together - the correct response's nu and its
    # variability, then the error's - rather than the two nus first.
    "cogmod_lnr" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmazero", "sigmaone", "sigmabias")] <-
        c("Nu (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Errors)",
          "Start Point Range")
      first <- c("Error Rate", "Mean RT", "Median RT", "mu", "sigmazero", "nuone", "sigmaone")
      lvls <- lvls[c(first, setdiff(names(lvls), first))]
    },
    # Both racing families: mu is the drift of the accumulator for correct
    # responses and driftone that of the other one, and sigmabias is the
    # start-point range A rather than a variability around a bias
    "cogmod_rdm" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias")] <- c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range")
    },
    "cogmod_lba2" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias", "sigmazero", "sigmaone")] <-
        c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range",
          "Drift SD (Correct)", "Drift SD (Errors)")
    }
  )
  lvls
}

# Rename the parameters and put them in canonical order. Parameter_Order keeps
# that order recoverable once the models are stacked together, where the factor
# levels of families that do not share their parameters get merged in whatever
# order the models happen to come in. It is the position in the full map rather
# than among the parameters this model has, so that it is comparable between
# models of a family that do not estimate the same ones.
format_parameters <- function(pred, family) {
  lvls <- param_labels(family)
  found <- unique(as.character(pred$Parameter))
  # A parameter the map does not know about (a family added later) keeps its
  # own name and goes last, rather than silently becoming an NA panel
  unknown <- setdiff(found, names(lvls))
  if (length(unknown) > 0) lvls <- c(lvls, setNames(unknown, unknown))
  pred$Parameter_Order <- match(as.character(pred$Parameter), names(lvls))
  lvls <- lvls[names(lvls) %in% found]

  pred$Parameter <- factor(unname(lvls[as.character(pred$Parameter)]),
                           levels = unname(lvls))
  pred
}

# The predictions of each of an illusion's models, relabelled, back in raw
# units, and stacked. Adding a model to `models` in the loading chunk is all it
# takes for it to get its own column in every plot below.
tidy_predictions <- function(preds, what) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(preds, \(p, name) {
    p[[what]] |>
      format_parameters(p$meta$family) |>
      # Restore the original scale of the illusion strength and difference
      restore_units(illusion = p$meta$illusion) |>
      mutate(Model = name, Family = p$meta$family)
  }) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(preds)))
}

# Parameters against illusion strength, one curve per illusion difficulty
# (compute_curves() in server/predictions.R), one data frame per illusion
preds_curves <- lapply(preds, tidy_predictions, what = "curves")

# The curves are predicted at 9 difficulty levels since 2026-11-16 (5 before).
# The Best Model draws all of them; the parameter curves of every model keep 5,
# every other level, which are the 5 of before. So a file of either kind gives
# the same parameter curves, and a mix of both works too. Pass the difference
# rounded, as levels from the two grids differ in the last digits.
coarse_levels <- function(x, n = 5) {
  lv <- sort(unique(x))
  if (length(lv) <= n) return(lv)
  lv[round(seq(1, length(lv), length.out = n))]
}
```



### Visualize

```{r}
# Column header
make_header <- function(label) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0, y = 0,
      label = label,
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 5
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
    theme_void()
}

# Height of the column-header row, in units of one panel row. A figure that
# puts something alongside the grid has to skip the headers to line up with the
# panels, so this is a shared constant rather than a default buried in the
# function below.
parameter_grid_header <- 0.35

# Which parameter goes in which row of which column. Models of one family share
# their parameters, so within a family rows are matched by name: the family's
# rows are every parameter any of its models has, in canonical order, and a
# model that does not estimate one (DDM-4's drift variability, say) gets a gap
# there. Families do not share them, so across families rows cannot be matched
# by name: each family's rows are packed from the top (which lines up the drift
# rates and the nus, both "mu"), and the non-decision time - the one parameter
# every family has - is anchored to the bottom row. The exception is a
# parameter that means the same thing in several families (`align`, the
# start-point range of the racing models): it goes in the same row everywhere,
# the lowest it falls in any family, with gaps above it in the others. Shorter
# columns get NA in between, drawn as spacers, so the columns stay aligned
# however many parameters they have.
parameter_grid_rows <- function(data, anchor_bottom = c("NDT", "NDT Variability"),
                                align = "Start Point Range") {
  data$Model <- droplevels(factor(data$Model))
  # Data without a family (made by hand, say) treats each model as its own
  if (is.null(data$Family)) data$Family <- as.character(data$Model)

  in_order <- function(d) unique(as.character(d$Parameter[order(d$Parameter_Order)]))
  families <- lapply(split(data, data$Family), \(d) {
    rows <- in_order(d)
    rows[!rows %in% anchor_bottom]
  })
  # Pad the families' top rows so that each aligned parameter lands in the row
  # of the family where it comes lowest
  for (p in align) {
    target <- max(0, unlist(lapply(families, \(rows) match(p, rows))), na.rm = TRUE)
    families <- lapply(families, \(rows) {
      at <- match(p, rows)
      if (is.na(at) || at == target) return(rows)
      append(rows, rep(NA_character_, target - at), after = at - 1)
    })
  }

  slots <- lapply(levels(data$Model), function(model) {
    family <- data$Family[data$Model == model][1]
    family_rows <- in_order(data[data$Family == family, ])
    own <- in_order(data[data$Model == model, ])
    top <- families[[family]]
    bottom <- family_rows[family_rows %in% anchor_bottom]
    list(top = ifelse(top %in% own, top, NA_character_),
         bottom = ifelse(bottom %in% own, bottom, NA_character_))
  })
  names(slots) <- levels(data$Model)
  n_top <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "top")))
  n_bottom <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "bottom")))

  lapply(slots, function(s) {
    c(s$top, rep(NA_character_, n_top - length(s$top)),
      rep(NA_character_, n_bottom - length(s$bottom)), s$bottom)
  })
}

# One column per model, one row per parameter, with panel(model, parameter)
# drawing each cell. The cells go into a single grid, filled column by column,
# rather than one sub-layout per model put side by side: patchwork only aligns
# panels within a layout, so separate columns let each one's rows drift with
# its own titles and legends.
plot_parameter_grid <- function(data, panel,
                                anchor_bottom = c("NDT", "NDT Variability"),
                                header_height = parameter_grid_header) {
  rows_by_model <- parameter_grid_rows(data, anchor_bottom)
  cells <- unlist(Map(function(model, rows) {
    c(list(make_header(model)),
      lapply(rows, function(p) if (is.na(p)) plot_spacer() else panel(model, p)))
  }, names(rows_by_model), rows_by_model), recursive = FALSE)

  wrap_plots(cells, ncol = length(rows_by_model), byrow = FALSE,
             heights = c(header_height, rep(1, length(rows_by_model[[1]]))))
}

# The curves of one illusion's models, from one element of preds_curves
plot_curves <- function(preds_curves) {
  # Prepare data
  curves <- preds_curves |>
    filter(!Parameter %in% c("Error Rate", "Mean RT", "Median RT")) |>
    # Rounded, or the levels print their floating-point error (0.0500000000001)
    mutate(Illusion_Difference = round(Illusion_Difference, 5)) |>
    filter(Illusion_Difference %in% coarse_levels(Illusion_Difference)) |>
    mutate(Illusion_Difference = factor(Illusion_Difference))

  # Colour scale
  curve_cols <- colorRampPalette(
    c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50")
  )(nlevels(curves$Illusion_Difference))

  # Function for individual panels
  make_curve <- function(model, parameter) {
    ggplot(
      filter(curves, Model == model, Parameter == parameter),
      aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted, colour = Illusion_Difference)
    ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = curve_cols) +
      labs(title = parameter, color = "Task Difficulty") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(
          hjust = 0.5,
          size = 11,
          margin = margin(b = 4)
        ),
        axis.title = element_blank()
      )
  }

  plot_parameter_grid(curves, make_curve) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
    )
}
```

### Visualize

```{r}
# Two ways of reading the values off the map: a colour bar per panel, or, as on
# an elevation map, the value written on a handful of the contour lines (which
# makes the colour bars redundant, so they are dropped)
heatmap_labels <- TRUE

# The linear-approximation region: the part of the space, in raw units, where
# the effects of the two predictors might be close enough to linear for a
# simpler model (~ Task_Difficulty * Illusion_Strength) fitted there to
# approximate the GAM, i.e. away from the extremes where they turn
# non-monotonic. Outlined on every heatmap panel, and the range of the colour
# gradient in the Best Model plots. An illusion without one gets no outline,
# and its whole range on the gradient.
#
# The Muller-Lyer box was drawn by eye. The other two are PROPOSED (2026-11-16)
# from it: the largest box, in trials kept, whose DDM-5 parameters are at least
# as close to bilinear as they are in the Muller-Lyer box. Bilinear means fitted
# by a + b*D + c*S + d*D*S on each parameter's link scale, over the
# heatmap grid; the Muller-Lyer box gets R2 >= 0.85 for every parameter (drift
# variability the worst) and keeps 63% of its trials. The curvature is almost
# all at extreme strengths, so the boxes cut there first:
# - Vertical-Horizontal: no difficulty cut, strengths beyond 45 dropped. 96% of
#   trials, worst R2 0.87 (bias).
# - Ebbinghaus: the two hardest levels (0.05, 0.07) and strengths beyond 1.5
#   dropped. 88% of trials, worst R2 0.86 (drift variability). With no
#   difficulty cut: 97.5%, R2 0.84.
linear_regions <- list(
  MullerLyer = list(strength = c(-30, 30), difference = c(0.1, 0.4)),
  VerticalHorizontal = list(strength = c(-45, 45), difference = c(0.03, 0.30)),
  Ebbinghaus = list(strength = c(-1.5, 1.5), difference = c(0.08, 0.70))
)

# Function for individual panels. The illusion is passed along for the
# outline, which is in its raw units.
make_heatmap <- function(preds_heatmaps, model, parameter, illusion) {
  d <- filter(preds_heatmaps, Model == model, Parameter == parameter)
  region <- linear_regions[[illusion]]
  contours <- if (heatmap_labels) {
    list(
      # Few enough lines that the labels have room: 20 would overlap in panels
      # this short. Breaks strictly inside the range, as pretty() can overshoot.
      geomtextpath::geom_textcontour(
        # The label is given explicitly: the default rounds it, which writes
        # 0.4 on every NDT contour from 0.37 to 0.41. The sign is a true minus
        # (U+2212): geomtextpath 0.2.0 silently drops an ASCII hyphen, which
        # labels -3 as 3 and makes the colour scale look reversed.
        aes(z = Predicted,
            label = after_stat(sub("^-", "−", format(level, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)))),
        breaks = (\(b) b[b > min(d$Predicted) & b < max(d$Predicted)])(pretty(d$Predicted, n = 10)),
        size = 2.5, linecolour = "white", textcolour = "white", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5,
        padding = grid::unit(0.5, "mm"), straight = TRUE
      ),
      guides(fill = "none")
    )
  } else {
    geom_contour(aes(z = Predicted), color = "white", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.5, bins = 20)
  }

  ggplot(d, aes(x = Illusion_Strength, y = Illusion_Difference)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Predicted)) +
    contours +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    (if (!is.null(region)) {
      annotate("rect", xmin = region$strength[1], xmax = region$strength[2],
               ymin = region$difference[1], ymax = region$difference[2],
               fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dotted")
    }) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = parameter, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.25, "cm"),
      # A null height stretches the colour bar to the height of its panel, so
      # it can neither overflow into the panel below nor sit off-centre
      legend.key.height = grid::unit(1, "null"),
      legend.ticks = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7)
    )
}

# Every panel shares the same axes, so the titles are dropped from the panels
# (see make_heatmap) and written once around the whole grid, next to a strip of
# stimuli showing what each axis means. patchwork has no shared axis title: the
# titles and the images each get their own row/column of the layout (the
# plot.tag route needs two nested wrap_elements, which renders the grid blank in
# patchwork 1.3.2).
axis_title <- function(label, rot = 0) {
  wrap_elements(grid::textGrob(label, rot = rot, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 13)))
}

# Stimuli along each axis, rendered by illustrations/make_illustrations.py
# (re-run it if the stimulus bounds change) as <illusion in lower case>_*.png.
# Both series are numbered low value to high, so they run in the direction of
# their axis: x left to right, y bottom to top, hence the reversal below. Only
# the Muller-Lyer has them so far; an illusion without them gets the grid and
# the axis titles alone.
illustrations_dir <- if (dir.exists("illustrations")) "illustrations" else "analysis/illustrations"
illustration_file <- function(illusion, name) {
  file.path(illustrations_dir, paste0(tolower(illusion), "_", name, ".png"))
}

# Every stimulus is drawn at the same size on both axes. The images already
# share their pixel dimensions (make_illustrations.py crops them with one box),
# so an explicit height is all it takes -- with the width left out, rasterGrob
# takes it from the aspect ratio. Letting each raster fill its cell instead
# would size the y-axis ones by the column width and the x-axis ones by the row
# height, which come out different once patchwork has taken its margins.
stim_h <- 1.55  # height of every stimulus, in inches
illustration <- function(illusion, name, vjust = "centre") {
  wrap_elements(grid::rasterGrob(
    png::readPNG(illustration_file(illusion, name)),
    # capped at the cell, so a figure too short for the strip shrinks it rather
    # than clipping it
    height = grid::unit.pmin(grid::unit(stim_h, "in"), grid::unit(1, "npc")),
    y = grid::unit(c(top = 1, centre = 0.5, bottom = 0)[[vjust]], "npc"),
    just = c("centre", vjust),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ))
}

# The heatmaps of one illusion's models, from one element of preds_heatmaps
plot_heatmaps <- function(preds_heatmaps, illusion) {
  # Each parameter is on its own scale, so unlike the curves the fill guides
  # cannot be collected: every panel keeps its own colour bar
  heatmaps <- plot_parameter_grid(
    preds_heatmaps,
    \(model, parameter) make_heatmap(preds_heatmaps, model, parameter, illusion)
  ) &
    theme(plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))

  # The y-axis column starts at the first panel, not at the column headers. The
  # row count is recomputed rather than carried out of plot_parameter_grid(): a
  # stale value here silently collapses the heights to an even split, which puts
  # the strip in the bottom half of the grid.
  grid_rows <- length(parameter_grid_rows(preds_heatmaps)[[1]])
  below_header <- function(p) {
    wrap_plots(plot_spacer(), p, ncol = 1, heights = c(parameter_grid_header, grid_rows))
  }

  # The strip and title rows/columns are sized in inches and the grid takes the
  # rest ("null"). Relative sizes would be read against the panels rather than
  # the cells, which leaves the strips adrift from the grid they annotate.
  if (!file.exists(illustration_file(illusion, "strength1"))) {
    return(wrap_plots(
      below_header(axis_title("Task Difficulty", rot = 90)), heatmaps,
      plot_spacer(), axis_title("Illusion Strength"),
      ncol = 2,
      widths = grid::unit(c(0.3, 1), c("in", "null")),
      heights = grid::unit(c(1, 0.3), c("null", "in"))
    ))
  }

  stim_aspect <- local({
    d <- dim(png::readPNG(illustration_file(illusion, "strength1")))
    d[2] / d[1]
  })
  # The outer two mark the ends of the y axis, so they sit flush with the top
  # and the bottom of the panel block rather than floating in the middle of
  # their cell
  y_strip <- wrap_plots(
    Map(\(name, vjust) illustration(illusion, name, vjust),
        paste0("difference", 3:1), c("top", "centre", "bottom")),
    ncol = 1
  )
  x_strip <- wrap_plots(lapply(paste0("strength", 1:3), \(name) illustration(illusion, name)), nrow = 1)

  wrap_plots(
    below_header(axis_title("Task Difficulty", rot = 90)), below_header(y_strip), heatmaps,
    plot_spacer(), plot_spacer(), x_strip,
    plot_spacer(), plot_spacer(), axis_title("Illusion Strength"),
    ncol = 3,
    widths = grid::unit(c(0.3, stim_h * stim_aspect + 0.2, 1), c("in", "in", "null")),
    heights = grid::unit(c(1, stim_h + 0.2, 0.3), c("null", "in", "in"))
  )
}
```

## Best Model

DDM-5, the one model that converged on all three illusions. Left: the error
rate and the median RT of correct responses that it predicts. Right: its
parameters. Every panel has every predicted difficulty level. The red to green
gradient spans the linear-approximation region outlined on the heatmaps (where
there is one). Beyond it the gradient carries on, faded: into purple for harder
levels, into cyan for easier ones.

```{r}
# The colour and the transparency of each task difficulty level (`levels`,
# sorted), each placed by its value on one gradient. Its red to green middle
# runs over the difficulty range of the linear-approximation region
# (linear_regions, with the heatmaps), red at the hard edge and green at the
# easy one. Outside it the gradient carries on, faded: from the red through
# pink to purple at the hardest level, and from the green through teal to cyan
# at the easiest. An illusion with no region has its whole range on the middle.
difficulty_scale <- function(levels, region = NULL) {
  bounds <- if (is.null(region)) range(levels) else region$difference
  # Tolerance for levels on the bounds, which carry floating-point error
  below <- levels < bounds[1] - 1e-8
  above <- levels > bounds[2] + 1e-8
  inside <- !below & !above

  middle <- grDevices::colorRamp(c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50"))
  harder <- grDevices::colorRamp(c("#FF5722", "#E91E63", "#9C27B0"))
  easier <- grDevices::colorRamp(c("#4CAF50", "#009688", "#00BCD4"))
  hex <- \(m) grDevices::rgb(m, maxColorValue = 255)

  cols <- hex(middle((pmin(pmax(levels, bounds[1]), bounds[2]) - bounds[1]) / diff(bounds)))
  if (any(below)) {
    cols[below] <- hex(harder((bounds[1] - levels[below]) / (bounds[1] - min(levels))))
  }
  if (any(above)) {
    cols[above] <- hex(easier((levels[above] - bounds[2]) / (max(levels) - bounds[2])))
  }
  list(colour = setNames(cols, levels),
       alpha = setNames(ifelse(inside, 1, 0.5), levels),
       inside = setNames(inside, levels))
}

# One element of preds_curves, i.e. one illusion, whose name is passed along
# for its linear-approximation region. A prediction file made before
# 2026-11-16 has no median RT and 5 difficulty levels: it shows the mean RT
# instead, at those 5 levels. Its chunks have warning: false for the RT, which
# is NA where a level predicts (almost) no correct responses, and ggplot says
# so once per layer.
plot_best_model <- function(preds_curves, illusion, model = "DDM-5") {
  # A model left out of an illusion's list (not converged, still fitting) has
  # no curves there
  if (!model %in% preds_curves$Model) {
    return(cat(model, "is not among this illusion's models.\n"))
  }
  d <- preds_curves |>
    filter(Model == model) |>
    mutate(Illusion_Difference = round(Illusion_Difference, 5))
  rt <- if ("Median RT" %in% d$Parameter) "Median RT" else "Mean RT"
  d <- d |>
    filter(!Parameter %in% setdiff(c("Mean RT", "Median RT"), rt)) |>
    # Panels in canonical order, the two outcomes first
    arrange(Parameter_Order) |>
    mutate(Parameter = factor(as.character(Parameter), levels = unique(as.character(Parameter))))

  # Left column: the error rate above the RT, half the height each. Right
  # column: one row per parameter, however many the model has.
  n_par <- nlevels(d$Parameter) - 2
  design <- matrix(c(rep(1:2, each = n_par), rep(seq_len(n_par) + 2, each = 2)), ncol = 2)

  region <- linear_regions[[illusion]]
  lv <- sort(unique(d$Illusion_Difference))
  sc <- difficulty_scale(lv, region)
  d$Inside <- sc$inside[as.character(d$Illusion_Difference)]
  d$Illusion_Difference <- factor(d$Illusion_Difference, levels = lv)

  # Two layers, so that the faded lines are drawn under the others rather than
  # over them. The colour and alpha scales share their title and levels, so
  # ggplot merges them into one legend, with faded keys. The breaks are given,
  # or the legend lists the levels in the order the layers bring them in, and
  # the labels rounded (0.06375 otherwise, on the Vertical-Horizontal).
  level_labels <- \(x) signif(as.numeric(x), 2)
  # The strengths outside the region, shaded: the curves only show its
  # difficulty bounds otherwise
  outside <- if (!is.null(region)) {
    data.frame(xmin = c(-Inf, region$strength[2]), xmax = c(region$strength[1], Inf)) |>
      filter(xmax > min(d$Illusion_Strength), xmin < max(d$Illusion_Strength))
  }
  ggplot(d, aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted, color = Illusion_Difference,
                alpha = Illusion_Difference, group = Illusion_Difference)) +
    (if (!is.null(outside) && nrow(outside) > 0) {
      geom_rect(data = outside, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey50", alpha = 0.12)
    }) +
    geom_line(data = \(x) filter(x, !Inside), linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_line(data = \(x) filter(x, Inside), linewidth = 1.1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = sc$colour, breaks = names(sc$colour), labels = level_labels) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = sc$alpha, breaks = names(sc$alpha), labels = level_labels) +
    ggh4x::facet_manual(vars(Parameter), design = design, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = model,
         subtitle = if (!is.null(region)) {
           paste0("Linear-approximation region: task difficulty ", region$difference[1],
                  " to ", region$difference[2], ", illusion strength ", region$strength[1],
                  " to ", region$strength[2], " (shaded outside)")
         },
         x = "Illusion Strength", y = NULL,
         color = "Task Difficulty", alpha = "Task Difficulty") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## Figures for the Paper

The figures of Study 1 in `paper/manuscript.qmd`, saved to `paper/figures/`.
The manuscript includes these files and computes nothing itself, so a change
in the fits reaches the paper by re-rendering this script. The tables of the
paper are figures too, drawn here: coloured cells are easier to read than a
grid of numbers, and a figure is laid out the same way in every output format.

```{r}
# Where the figures go, and how they are saved. PNG at 300 dpi: the manuscript
# is set in LaTeX, Word or Typst from the same source, and all three take it.
paper_dir <- if (dir.exists("../paper")) "../paper/figures/" else "paper/figures/"
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width, height) {
  dir.create(paper_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ggsave(paste0(paper_dir, name, ".png"), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white", device = ragg::agg_png)
  plot
}

# The order and the names used in the paper: the diffusion models first, then
# the race models, each plain model followed by its start-point-range variant.
paper_models <- c("DDM-4", "DDM-5", "LNR", "LNR-6", "RDM", "RDM-5", "LBA")
paper_illusions <- c(MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer", VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal",
                     Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus")
paper_families <- c("DDM-4" = "Diffusion", "DDM-5" = "Diffusion", "LNR" = "Race", "LNR-6" = "Race",
                    "RDM" = "Race", "RDM-5" = "Race", "LBA" = "Race")
retained_model <- "DDM-5"

# The table figures share one look: tiles with a white grid between them, the
# column names above, no axis furniture
theme_table <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.title = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x.top = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size - 1, lineheight = 0.9,
                                         vjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 2)),
          axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1, hjust = 0.5,
                                    margin = margin(b = 1)),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = base_size - 1.5, hjust = 0.5,
                                       margin = margin(b = 3)),
          strip.text = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(5, "pt"),
          legend.position = "none",
          plot.margin = margin(2, 3, 2, 3))
}
num <- \(x, digits = 0) sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ","))
```

### The Models

What each of the seven models estimates, under two schematics of how the two
families work. The table is read from the prediction files: a parameter with
curves is one that was given a smooth.

```{r}
# The processes a model can have, in the order of the table's columns, with the
# colour each keeps in the schematics and in the table
components <- data.frame(
  Component = c("rate", "ratevar", "boundary", "start", "startrange", "ndt"),
  Label = c("Evidence rate", "Rate variability", "Boundary", "Starting point",
            "Start-point range", "Non-decision time"),
  Header = c("Evidence<br>rate", "Rate<br>variability", "Boundary", "Starting<br>point",
             "Start-point<br>range", "Non-decision<br>time"),
  # What each one means, for the reader who does not know these models
  Gloss = c("how fast evidence<br>builds up", "how much it varies<br>between trials",
            "how much evidence<br>is needed", "an initial lean<br>to one response",
            "how much it varies<br>between trials", "time to see, and<br>to press the key"),
  Colour = c("#1E88E5", "#00ACC1", "#8E24AA", "#FB8C00", "#F4511E", "#757575")
)
component_colours <- setNames(components$Colour, components$Component)

# Which of its family's parameters belongs to which process. A parameter listed
# here that a model does not estimate was fixed (models.R); a process with no
# parameter is not part of that family.
family_components <- list(
  cogmod_ddm = c(mu = "rate", sigmadrift = "ratevar", boundary = "boundary", bias = "start",
                 sigmabias = "startrange", ndt = "ndt"),
  cogmod_lnr = c(mu = "rate", nuone = "rate", sigmazero = "ratevar", sigmaone = "ratevar",
                 sigmabias = "startrange", ndt = "ndt"),
  cogmod_rdm = c(mu = "rate", driftone = "rate", boundary = "boundary",
                 sigmabias = "startrange", ndt = "ndt"),
  cogmod_lba2 = c(mu = "rate", driftone = "rate", sigmazero = "ratevar", sigmaone = "ratevar",
                  boundary = "boundary", sigmabias = "startrange", ndt = "ndt")
)
accumulation <- c(cogmod_ddm = "noisy diffusion", cogmod_lnr = "lognormal finishing times",
                  cogmod_rdm = "noisy diffusion", cogmod_lba2 = "linear (ballistic)")

# What each model estimates, read from its prediction files: the parameters it
# has curves for are the ones given a smooth
model_table <- function(preds) {
  fits <- unlist(unname(preds), recursive = FALSE)
  fits <- fits[!duplicated(names(fits))]
  purrr::imap_dfr(fits[paper_models], \(p, model) {
    map <- family_components[[p$meta$family]]
    free <- intersect(unique(p$curves$Parameter), names(map))
    components |>
      mutate(Model = model, Family = p$meta$family,
             N_family = vapply(Component, \(k) sum(map == k), numeric(1)),
             N_free = vapply(Component, \(k) sum(map[free] == k), numeric(1)),
             N_total = length(free))
  }) |>
    mutate(State = case_when(N_free > 0 ~ "free", N_family > 0 ~ "fixed", .default = "absent"),
           Text = case_when(State == "free" & N_family > 1 & N_free == N_family ~ "one per\naccumulator",
                            State == "free" & N_free < N_family ~ "error\naccumulator",
                            State == "free" ~ "✓", State == "fixed" ~ "fixed", .default = "–"))
}

# Panels A and B, the two architectures. The paths are simulated with fixed
# seeds, picked for paths that are easy to read, so the figure does not change
# from one render to the next.
simulate_path <- function(drift, start, bound, lower = -Inf, noise = 0.32, seed = 1, t0 = 0.4,
                          dt = 0.004, n = 600) {
  set.seed(seed)
  x <- start + cumsum(drift * dt + noise * sqrt(dt) * rnorm(n))
  hit <- which(x >= bound | x <= lower)[1]
  if (is.na(hit)) hit <- n
  x <- pmin(pmax(x[seq_len(hit)], lower), bound)
  data.frame(Time = t0 + c(0, seq_len(hit) * dt), Evidence = c(start, x))
}

schematic_theme <- function() {
  theme_void(base_size = 9) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 7.5, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 0.95,
                                       margin = margin(t = 2, b = 3)),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 2, 4))
}
# A label in the colour of its process, on a white halo so that it stays
# readable over the paths
note <- function(x, y, label, component, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) {
  # No border: ggplot2 4.0 renamed the argument that sets its width
  border <- if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "4.0.0") list(linewidth = 0) else list(label.size = 0)
  do.call(annotate, c(
    list("label", x = x, y = y, label = label, colour = component_colours[[component]],
         size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust, lineheight = 0.85,
         fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8), label.padding = grid::unit(1, "pt")),
    border))
}
# The correct response and the error, as lines and as text: the boundaries of
# the diffusion and the accumulators of the race
response_colours <- c(correct = "#43A047", error = "#E53935")
response_ink <- c(correct = "#2E7D32", error = "#C62828")
arrow_small <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(3.5, "pt"), type = "closed")
arrow_both <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(3.5, "pt"), type = "closed", ends = "both")
# What the two schematics share: the time axis and the boundary's height
schematic_frame <- function(t0, top) {
  list(
    annotate("segment", x = 1.62, xend = 1.62, y = 0, yend = top, linewidth = 0.5,
             colour = component_colours[["boundary"]], arrow = arrow_both),
    note(1.66, top / 2, "Boundary", "boundary", hjust = 0),
    annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 1.55, y = -0.2, yend = -0.2, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40",
             arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(3, "pt"))),
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.28, label = "Stimulus", hjust = 0, size = 2.5, colour = "grey40"),
    annotate("text", x = 1.55, y = -0.28, label = "Time", hjust = 1, size = 2.5, colour = "grey40"),
    annotate("point", x = 0, y = -0.2, size = 1, colour = "grey40"),
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.13, 2.02), ylim = c(-0.32, 1.13), expand = FALSE),
    schematic_theme()
  )
}

plot_schematic_diffusion <- function() {
  t0 <- 0.4; a <- 1; z <- 0.5; rate <- 0.6
  main <- simulate_path(rate, z, a, lower = 0, seed = 13, t0 = t0)
  # Two other trials, one of them an error
  other <- bind_rows(
    mutate(simulate_path(rate, z, a, lower = 0, seed = 32, t0 = t0), Path = "b"),
    mutate(simulate_path(-0.5, z, a, lower = 0, seed = 12, t0 = t0), Path = "c"))
  ggplot(main, aes(Time, Evidence)) +
    # The two boundaries in the colours of the two accumulators of the race
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = 1.55, y = c(0, a), yend = c(0, a), linewidth = 0.8,
             colour = response_colours[c("error", "correct")]) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.55, y = a + 0.06, label = "Correct response", hjust = 1, size = 2.6,
             colour = response_ink[["correct"]], fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 1.55, y = -0.07, label = "Error", hjust = 1, size = 2.6,
             colour = response_ink[["error"]], fontface = "bold") +
    geom_line(data = other, aes(group = Path), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = t0, y = z, yend = z, linewidth = 0.7, colour = component_colours[["ndt"]]) +
    # The rate is the average slope, and its variability a fan of slopes
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0 + 0.42, y = z, yend = z + 0.42 * c(0.15, 1.05), linewidth = 0.35,
             colour = component_colours[["ratevar"]], linetype = "22") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.45, colour = "grey15") +
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0 + 0.42, y = z, yend = z + 0.42 * rate, linewidth = 0.8,
             colour = component_colours[["rate"]], arrow = arrow_small) +
    note(t0 + 0.2, z + 0.37, "Evidence rate", "rate", hjust = 1) +
    annotate("segment", x = t0 + 0.2, xend = t0 + 0.3, y = z + 0.31, yend = z + 0.21, linewidth = 0.25,
             colour = component_colours[["rate"]]) +
    note(t0 + 0.46, z + 0.07, "Rate variability", "ratevar", hjust = 0) +
    # Starting point and its range
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0, y = z - 0.13, yend = z + 0.13, linewidth = 1.8,
             colour = component_colours[["startrange"]], alpha = 0.5) +
    annotate("point", x = t0, y = z, size = 1.8, colour = component_colours[["start"]]) +
    note(t0 - 0.04, z + 0.14, "Starting point", "start", hjust = 1) +
    note(t0 + 0.05, z - 0.19, "Start-point range", "startrange", hjust = 0) +
    note(t0 / 2 - 0.03, z - 0.12, "Non-decision\ntime", "ndt") +
    schematic_frame(t0, a) +
    labs(title = "Diffusion models (DDM)",
         subtitle = "One accumulator drifts between two boundaries:\nthe one it reaches is the response.")
}

plot_schematic_race <- function() {
  t0 <- 0.4; b <- 1
  correct <- simulate_path(0.95, 0.18, b, noise = 0.25, seed = 12, t0 = t0)
  error <- simulate_path(0.45, 0.07, b, noise = 0.25, seed = 150, t0 = t0)
  # The race stops when the first one arrives
  error <- error[error$Time <= max(correct$Time), ]
  ggplot(correct, aes(Time, Evidence)) +
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = 1.55, y = b, yend = b, linewidth = 0.7) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.55, y = b + 0.06, label = "Response", hjust = 1, size = 2.6) +
    annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = t0, y = 0.125, yend = 0.125, linewidth = 0.7,
             colour = component_colours[["ndt"]]) +
    geom_line(data = error, linewidth = 0.45, colour = response_colours[["error"]]) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.45, colour = response_colours[["correct"]]) +
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0 + 0.3, y = 0.18, yend = 0.18 + 0.3 * 0.95, linewidth = 0.8,
             colour = component_colours[["rate"]], arrow = arrow_small) +
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0 + 0.3, y = 0.07, yend = 0.07 + 0.3 * 0.45, linewidth = 0.8,
             colour = component_colours[["rate"]], arrow = arrow_small) +
    note(t0 + 0.06, 0.62, "Evidence rates", "rate", hjust = 1) +
    annotate("segment", x = t0 + 0.06, xend = t0 + 0.16, y = 0.56, yend = 0.4, linewidth = 0.25,
             colour = component_colours[["rate"]]) +
    annotate("text", x = max(correct$Time) - 0.3, y = 0.9, label = "Correct accumulator", hjust = 1,
             size = 2.5, colour = response_ink[["correct"]], fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 1.57, y = error$Evidence[nrow(error)] - 0.17, label = "Error accumulator",
             hjust = 1, size = 2.5, colour = response_ink[["error"]], fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("segment", x = t0, xend = t0, y = 0, yend = 0.25, linewidth = 1.8,
             colour = component_colours[["startrange"]], alpha = 0.5) +
    note(t0 + 0.05, -0.07, "Start-point range", "startrange", hjust = 0) +
    note(t0 / 2 - 0.03, 0.01, "Non-decision\ntime", "ndt") +
    schematic_frame(t0, b) +
    labs(title = "Race models (LNR, RDM, LBA)",
         subtitle = "One accumulator per response:\nthe first to reach the boundary gives the response.")
}

# Panel B, the table: one row per model, one column per process
plot_model_table <- function(tab) {
  tab <- tab |>
    mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = rev(paper_models)),
           Component = factor(Component, levels = components$Component),
           Group = factor(paper_families[as.character(Model)], levels = c("Diffusion", "Race")),
           Fill = case_when(State == "free" ~ scales::alpha(Colour, 0.85),
                            State == "fixed" ~ "#ECECEC", .default = "#FFFFFF"),
           Ink = case_when(State == "free" ~ "white", State == "fixed" ~ "grey35", .default = "grey60"))
  per_model <- distinct(tab, Model, Group, Family, N_total)

  ggplot(tab, aes(y = Model)) +
    geom_tile(aes(x = as.numeric(Component) + 2.6, fill = Fill), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_text(aes(x = as.numeric(Component) + 2.6, label = Text, colour = Ink,
                  size = ifelse(Text %in% c("✓", "–"), 3.6, 2.35)),
              lineheight = 0.8, fontface = "bold") +
    # Model names on their colour, how each accumulates, and how many of its
    # parameters are free
    geom_tile(data = per_model, aes(x = 0.5, fill = model_colors[as.character(Model)]),
              width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_text(data = per_model, aes(x = 0.5, label = Model), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = per_model, aes(x = 1.12, label = accumulation[Family]), hjust = 0, size = 2.6,
              colour = "grey20") +
    geom_text(data = per_model, aes(x = 9.5, label = N_total), fontface = "bold", size = 3.2) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_size_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 10),
                       breaks = c(0.5, 2.05, 3.6:8.6, 9.5),
                       labels = c("**Model**", "**Accumulation**",
                                  paste0("**", components$Header, "**<br><span style='font-size:5.5pt'>",
                                         components$Gloss, "</span>"),
                                  "**Total**")) +
    facet_grid(Group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    theme_table() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x.top = ggtext::element_markdown(
            size = 7.5, lineheight = 1.05, vjust = 0,
            colour = c("black", "black", components$Colour, "black")))
}

plot_models <- function(preds) {
  top <- wrap_plots(plot_schematic_diffusion(), plot_schematic_race(), nrow = 1)
  wrap_plots(top, plot_model_table(model_table(preds)), ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 1.05)) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
}
```

### Predictive Check

```{r}
# The posterior predictive check of the three illusions side by side, with one
# legend. plot_ppc() is the one of the section above. The legend of the models
# is taken from the panel that has the most of them: patchwork only merges
# legends that are identical, and an illusion with a model missing has another.
#
# The models differ most at the peak of the correct responses, where their
# lines are on top of each other on a plain axis. Two ways of pulling them
# apart:
# - `y_scale`: "square" stretches the high densities (and flattens the errors
#   and the tails), "sqrt" does the opposite, "linear" leaves the axis alone.
#   The transform is of the size of the density, so that errors stay mirrored.
# - `zoom`: two insets, with the peak of the correct responses and that of the
#   errors enlarged, and a frame around what each enlarges.
signed_power <- function(power) {
  scales::new_transform(paste0("signed_power_", power),
                        transform = \(x) sign(x) * abs(x)^power,
                        inverse = \(x) sign(x) * abs(x)^(1 / power))
}
plot_ppc_paper <- function(preds, y_scale = c("linear", "square", "sqrt"), zoom = FALSE) {
  y_scale <- match.arg(y_scale)
  preds <- lapply(preds, \(p) p[intersect(paper_models, names(p))])
  with_legend <- which.max(lengths(preds))
  panels <- lapply(seq_along(preds), \(i) {
    p <- plot_ppc(preds[[i]], rt_range = c(0, 2), linewidth = 0.45) +
      labs(title = paper_illusions[[names(preds)[i]]], x = "Response time (s)",
           y = if (i == 1) "Density" else NULL) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(alpha = 0.6)),
             color = if (i == with_legend) {
               guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 1, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1))
             } else {
               "none"
             }) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5, hjust = 0.5),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.25))
    if (y_scale != "linear") {
      p <- suppressMessages(
        p + scale_y_continuous(transform = signed_power(c(square = 2, sqrt = 0.5)[[y_scale]]),
                               breaks = c(-0.5, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), labels = abs)
      )
    }
    if (!zoom) return(p)

    # An inset is the same plot cut to a window, on a plain axis
    observed <- p$layers[[1]]$data
    predicted <- p$layers[[2]]$data
    top <- max(observed$y, predicted$y)
    inset <- function(window_x, window_y) {
      ggplotGrob(suppressMessages(
        p + scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
          coord_cartesian(xlim = window_x, ylim = range(window_y), expand = FALSE) +
          labs(title = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
          theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_blank(),
                panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4),
                plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
                plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
      ))
    }
    frame <- function(window_x, window_y) {
      annotate("rect", xmin = window_x[1], xmax = window_x[2], ymin = min(window_y), ymax = max(window_y),
               fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3)
    }

    # The peak of the correct responses: the observed mode, 0.12 s either
    # side, and the top quarter of the densities there. Its inset is in the
    # empty corner above the tail.
    correct_x <- observed$x[which.max(observed$y)] + c(-0.12, 0.12)
    correct_y <- c(0.72, 1.03) * top

    # The peak of the errors, which is wider and where the models differ more
    # in proportion: 0.15 s either side of where the models put it (the
    # observed histogram of the errors is too rough to give a mode), and the
    # lower half of the densities there. Its inset is under the axis, which is
    # extended to make room for it.
    errors <- filter(predicted, y < 0)
    error_mode <- errors |>
      summarise(x = x[which.min(y)], .by = Model) |>
      pull(x) |>
      median()
    error_x <- error_mode + c(-0.15, 0.15)
    depth <- min(errors$y, observed$y[observed$x > error_x[1] & observed$x < error_x[2]])
    error_y <- c(0.5, 1.04) * depth

    p +
      expand_limits(y = -0.59 * top) +
      frame(correct_x, correct_y) +
      frame(error_x, error_y) +
      annotation_custom(inset(correct_x, correct_y), xmin = 0.95, xmax = 2.05, ymin = 0.42 * top, ymax = 1.03 * top) +
      annotation_custom(inset(error_x, error_y), xmin = 0.95, xmax = 2.05, ymin = -0.58 * top, ymax = -0.13 * top)
  })
  wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", legend.margin = margin(t = -2),
          legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(0, "pt"), legend.key.size = grid::unit(10, "pt"),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8), legend.title = element_text(size = 8))
}
```

It is the lower half of the paper's comparison figure, saved with it below.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 3.7

# The paper has the zoom. A squared axis pulls the lines apart at the peak too,
# but flattens the errors and the tails to nothing; a square-root or log axis
# does the opposite of what is wanted (tried 2026-11-24).
plot_ppc_paper(preds, zoom = TRUE)
```
