### Convergence, Performance and Cost

The table of the model comparison: for every model and illusion, whether the
fit converged, how well it predicts against DDM-5, and what it cost.

```{r}
# One row per fit, with everything the paper reports about it. The ELPD
# difference is from the retained model on the same illusion, with the SE of
# the difference from the paired trial-wise values, as loo_compare() gives it.
summarise_fits <- function(preds, reference = retained_model) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(preds, \(fits, illusion) {
    ref <- fits[[reference]]$loo$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"]
    purrr::imap_dfr(fits, \(p, model) {
      cv <- p$convergence
      d <- p$loo$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"] - ref
      data.frame(
        Illusion = illusion, Model = model, Sampler = p$meta$sampler,
        Rhat = cv$rhat_pop_max, Rhat_lp = cv$rhat_lp, ESS = cv$ess_bulk_pop_min,
        Divergent_pct = cv$divergent_pct,
        ELPD = p$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"], ELPD_SE = p$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"],
        ELPD_diff = sum(d), ELPD_diff_SE = sqrt(length(d)) * sd(d),
        Pareto_k_pct = 100 * mean(p$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7),
        # Compute: how long a chain took on average, and the total over the
        # chains and their threads, which is what one core would have taken
        # (assuming threading scales linearly, server/AGENT.md 4.4.1)
        Chain_days = mean(p$efficiency$Time_total) / 86400,
        Core_days = sum(p$efficiency$Time_total * p$efficiency$Threads) / 86400,
        Core_hours = sum(p$efficiency$Time_total * p$efficiency$Threads) / 3600
      )
    })
  }) |>
    # The criteria of the paper (Evaluation), which are the "acceptable" ones
    # of the convergence tables above
    mutate(Converged = Rhat <= 1.05 & Rhat_lp <= 1.1 & ESS >= 100 & Divergent_pct < 1)
}

# How each fit that did not converge failed: the number of posterior modes its
# chains settled in and how the 8 chains divided between them, or a warmup that
# never adapted. This is read off the chains by hand, not computed
# (server/AGENT.md 4.10 B and C, and the comments in `models` above).
#
# LNR-6 on Ebbinghaus has no combined fit in this generation (cogmod 0.3.5,
# 1500 warmup + 1000 draws): three of its four jobs ran into the 8-day limit,
# and were not rerun because the one that finished had the adaptation failure
# of LNR on that illusion. The complete fit of it that exists is of the
# generation before (cogmod 0.3.4, 1000 + 500), archived at the 2026-10-13
# refit, and it failed in the same way (server/AGENT.md 4.10 C and 6.5). See
# `earlier_fits` below for what the figure takes from it.
failures <- c(
  "LNR-6 MullerLyer" = "2 modes (4:4)", "RDM-5 MullerLyer" = "2 modes (6:2)",
  "LBA MullerLyer" = "2 modes (6:2)", "RDM-5 VerticalHorizontal" = "2 modes (6:2)",
  "LBA VerticalHorizontal" = "4 modes", "LBA Ebbinghaus" = "2 modes (6:2)",
  "LNR Ebbinghaus" = "failed warmup", "LNR-6 Ebbinghaus" = "failed warmup"
)

# A model with no complete fit in this generation, but one in the generation
# before: its convergence cell is filled from that fit, and marked. Nothing
# else can be taken from it. That fit is of other data (the block exclusions
# changed on 2026-10-12: 320,144 trials against 316,487), with other priors
# (cogmod 0.3.4) and a shorter run, so its ELPD cannot be set against DDM-5's
# and its cost is not that of the others. Its prediction file is read as it
# is, without load_predictions(), which is for the current generation.
earlier_fits <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  list(Model = "LNR-6", Illusion = "Ebbinghaus",
       File = "old_20261004/gam_lnr6_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus.rds"),
  \(Model, Illusion, File) {
    if (!file.exists(paste0(pred_path, File))) return(NULL)
    cv <- readRDS(paste0(pred_path, File))$convergence
    data.frame(Model = Model, Illusion = Illusion, Rhat_earlier = cv$rhat_pop_max,
               Converged_earlier = cv$rhat_pop_max <= 1.05 & cv$rhat_lp <= 1.1 &
                 cv$ess_bulk_pop_min >= 100 & cv$divergent_pct < 1)
  }
)

plot_comparison <- function(fits, earlier = earlier_fits) {
  if (is.null(earlier) || nrow(earlier) == 0) {
    earlier <- data.frame(Model = character(), Illusion = character(), Rhat_earlier = numeric(),
                          Converged_earlier = logical())
  }
  d <- expand.grid(Model = paper_models, Illusion = names(paper_illusions), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    left_join(fits, by = c("Model", "Illusion")) |>
    left_join(earlier, by = c("Model", "Illusion")) |>
    mutate(Failure = failures[paste(Model, Illusion)],
           Fitted = !is.na(Rhat),
           # No fit in this generation, but one in the one before
           Earlier = !Fitted & !is.na(Rhat_earlier),
           Group = factor(paper_families[Model], levels = c("Diffusion", "Race")),
           Model = factor(Model, levels = rev(paper_models)),
           Illusion = factor(paper_illusions[Illusion], levels = paper_illusions),
           Retained = Model == retained_model)
  if (any(d$Fitted & !d$Converged & is.na(d$Failure))) {
    stop("A fit that did not converge has no entry in `failures`.")
  }

  panel <- function(fill, top, bottom, ink, title, subtitle) {
    ggplot(d, aes(Illusion, Model)) +
      geom_tile(aes(fill = {{ fill }}), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
      geom_tile(data = \(x) filter(x, Retained), fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5,
                width = 0.96, height = 0.92) +
      geom_text(aes(label = {{ top }}, colour = {{ ink }}), size = 2.9, fontface = "bold", nudge_y = 0.17) +
      geom_text(data = \(x) filter(x, !grepl("\n", {{ bottom }})),
                aes(label = {{ bottom }}, colour = {{ ink }}), size = 2.2, nudge_y = -0.2) +
      # A second line of two rows (the fit with no combined fit) has the cell
      # to itself, and is centred in it
      geom_text(data = \(x) filter(x, grepl("\n", {{ bottom }})),
                aes(label = {{ bottom }}, colour = {{ ink }}), size = 2.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
      scale_fill_identity() +
      scale_colour_identity() +
      scale_x_discrete(position = "top", expand = c(0, 0), labels = \(x) sub("-", "-\n", x)) +
      scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      facet_grid(Group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
      labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
      theme_table() +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  }

  # Convergence: green if the chains agree, red if not, with the largest Rhat
  # and, under it, the smallest effective sample size or the kind of failure
  d <- d |>
    mutate(Conv_fill = case_when(Earlier & Converged_earlier ~ "#B7E1BB", Earlier ~ "#F2A6A0",
                                 !Fitted ~ "#E0E0E0", Converged ~ "#B7E1BB", .default = "#F2A6A0"),
           Conv_top = case_when(Earlier ~ paste0(formatC(Rhat_earlier, format = "f", digits = 3), "‡"),
                                Fitted ~ formatC(Rhat, format = "f", digits = 3), .default = ""),
           Conv_bottom = case_when(Earlier ~ Failure,
                                   !Fitted ~ paste0(Failure, "\n(not completed)"),
                                   Converged ~ paste("ESS", num(ESS)), .default = Failure),
           Conv_ink = ifelse(Fitted | Earlier, "black", "grey35"))

  # Predictive performance: blue where the model predicts better than the
  # retained one and brown where worse, on a square-root scale so that the
  # small differences keep some colour. A fit that did not converge is faded
  # and marked: its ELPD is that of a mixture of modes.
  ramp <- scales::colour_ramp(c("#A6611A", "#DFC27D", "#F7F7F7", "#80B7D8", "#2B6CA3"))
  signed_sqrt <- \(x) sign(x) * sqrt(abs(x))
  limit <- max(abs(signed_sqrt(d$ELPD_diff)), na.rm = TRUE)
  d <- d |>
    mutate(Perf_fill = case_when(!Fitted ~ "#E0E0E0",
                                 !Converged ~ scales::alpha(ramp((signed_sqrt(ELPD_diff) / limit + 1) / 2), 0.35),
                                 .default = ramp((signed_sqrt(ELPD_diff) / limit + 1) / 2)),
           Perf_top = case_when(!Fitted ~ "–", Retained ~ "0",
                                .default = paste0(ifelse(ELPD_diff > 0, "+", ""), num(ELPD_diff),
                                                  ifelse(Converged, "", "†"))),
           Perf_bottom = case_when(!Fitted ~ "", Retained ~ paste0("ELPD ", num(ELPD)),
                                   .default = paste0("± ", num(ELPD_diff_SE))),
           Perf_ink = case_when(!Fitted | !Converged ~ "grey45",
                                abs(signed_sqrt(ELPD_diff)) / limit > 0.75 ~ "white", .default = "black"))

  # Computational cost, darker when dearer: how long a chain took, in days,
  # which is what one waits for, and under it the total in months of one core
  cost <- scales::colour_ramp(c("#F3F0F7", "#7E6BAD"))
  d <- d |>
    mutate(Cost_fill = ifelse(Fitted, cost(scales::rescale(Core_days, from = c(0, max(Core_days, na.rm = TRUE)))),
                              "#E0E0E0"),
           Cost_top = ifelse(Fitted, paste(num(Chain_days, 1), "days"), "–"),
           Cost_bottom = ifelse(Fitted, paste(num(Core_days / (365.25 / 12), 1), "months"), ""),
           Cost_ink = ifelse(Fitted & Core_days > 0.8 * max(Core_days, na.rm = TRUE), "white", "black"))

  # The model names, on their colours, once for the three panels
  names_panel <- ggplot(distinct(d, Model, Group), aes(1, Model)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = model_colors[as.character(Model)]), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Model), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", expand = c(0, 0), breaks = 1, labels = "") +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    facet_grid(Group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    labs(title = "", subtitle = "") +
    theme_table() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90, size = 8, colour = "grey30", face = "bold"))

  wrap_plots(
    names_panel,
    panel(Conv_fill, Conv_top, Conv_bottom, Conv_ink, "Convergence",
          expression("largest " * hat(R) * ", and smallest ESS or failure")),
    panel(Perf_fill, Perf_top, Perf_bottom, Perf_ink, "Predictive performance",
          expression(Delta * "ELPD from DDM-5 (higher is better)")),
    panel(Cost_fill, Cost_top, Cost_bottom, Cost_ink, "Computational cost",
          "days per chain, and total months of one core"),
    nrow = 1, widths = c(0.42, 1, 1, 1)
  )
}

# The figure of the paper: that table over the predictive check.
# Each half is wrapped whole, so that it keeps its own layout and legend, and
# gets one tag
plot_comparison_ppc <- function(fits, preds) {
  wrap_plots(wrap_elements(full = plot_comparison(fits)),
             wrap_elements(full = plot_ppc_paper(preds, zoom = TRUE)),
             ncol = 1, heights = c(3.9, 3.6)) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
}
```

### The Retained Model

```{r}
# The retained model on the three illusions: what it predicts (error rate and
# median RT of correct responses), then its parameters. Two of them are turned
# around for the reader. The fits code an error as the upper boundary, so their
# drift is negative when it goes towards the correct response, and their bias
# is the distance of the starting point from the correct boundary. Here the
# drift is positive towards the correct response, and the starting point is 0
# at the error boundary and 1 at the correct one.
plot_retained <- function(preds_curves, model = retained_model) {
  # The rows, in two groups: what can be observed, and what the model explains
  # it with
  groups <- list(
    "Observable Outcomes" = c("Error Rate" = "Error rate", "Median RT" = "Median RT\n(correct, s)"),
    "Model Parameters" = c("Drift" = "Drift rate\n(+ towards correct)", "Drift Variability" = "Drift rate\nvariability",
                           "Boundary" = "Boundary\nseparation", "Bias" = "Starting point\n(0 error, 1 correct)",
                           "NDT" = "Non-decision\ntime (s)")
  )
  panels <- unlist(unname(groups))
  d <- purrr::imap_dfr(preds_curves, \(x, illusion) {
    x |>
      filter(Model == model, Parameter %in% names(panels)) |>
      mutate(Illusion = illusion,
             # The difficulty levels differ between illusions: their rank is
             # what is coloured, from the hardest to the easiest
             Difficulty = dense_rank(round(Illusion_Difference, 5)),
             Difficulty = (Difficulty - 1) / (max(Difficulty) - 1))
  }) |>
    mutate(Predicted = case_when(Parameter == "Drift" ~ -Predicted,
                                 Parameter == "Bias" ~ 1 - Predicted,
                                 .default = Predicted),
           Parameter = panels[as.character(Parameter)],
           Illusion = factor(paper_illusions[Illusion], levels = paper_illusions))

  # Reference lines: no drift, and a starting point half-way
  refs <- data.frame(Parameter = panels[c("Drift", "Bias")], y = c(0, 0.5))

  # One group of rows. The groups are plots of their own, one above the other,
  # so that there is a gap between them. Their columns line up, so the
  # illusions are named once, above the first, and the axis of illusion
  # strength is drawn once, under the last.
  block <- function(name) {
    rows <- groups[[name]]
    first <- name == names(groups)[1]
    last <- name == names(groups)[length(groups)]
    in_block <- \(x) mutate(filter(x, Parameter %in% rows), Parameter = factor(Parameter, levels = rows))
    ggplot(in_block(d), aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_hline(data = in_block(refs), aes(yintercept = y), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3,
                 linetype = "dashed") +
      geom_line(aes(colour = Difficulty, group = Difficulty), linewidth = 0.55, na.rm = TRUE) +
      scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#D84315", "#FF9800", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#2E7D32"),
                             limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 1), labels = c("hardest", "easiest"),
                             guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "left", barwidth = grid::unit(6, "lines"),
                                                     barheight = grid::unit(0.5, "lines"))) +
      facet_grid(Parameter ~ Illusion, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
      labs(y = NULL, colour = "Task difficulty ",
           x = if (last) "Illusion strength (negative: congruent, positive: incongruent)") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
      theme(strip.placement = "outside",
            strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 8, lineheight = 0.9),
            strip.text.x = if (first) element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5) else element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
            panel.spacing = grid::unit(7, "pt"),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
            axis.text.x = if (last) element_text(size = 7) else element_blank(),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 8, vjust = 0.9),
            legend.margin = margin(t = -4),
            plot.margin = margin(if (first) 4 else 9, 4, 4, 2))
  }

  # The name of a group, written upwards on a band at the left of its rows.
  # patchwork lines its panel up with the panels of the group, so the band is
  # as tall as the rows and no taller.
  band <- function(name) {
    first <- name == names(groups)[1]
    ggplot() +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = name, angle = 90, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, colour = "grey15") +
      theme_void() +
      theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey91", colour = NA),
            plot.margin = margin(if (first) 4 else 9, 0, 4, 2))
  }

  wrap_plots(unlist(lapply(names(groups), \(name) list(band(name), block(name))), recursive = FALSE),
             ncol = 2, widths = c(0.035, 1), heights = lengths(groups), guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

### Every Model

The parameters of all seven models at once, as surfaces over the two
manipulations. The models do not share their parameters, so the rows are the
processes of the models figure, with the two accumulators of a race in
separate rows. A model without a process leaves its cell empty. The drift and
the starting point of the DDM are turned around as in the figure of the
retained model. The fits that did not converge are drawn like the others:
which ones they are is in the comparison figure, and in the note of this one
in the manuscript.

```{r}
# The rows of the grid: a process and, for the rate and its variability, the
# accumulator. A race model has a rate towards each response, one per
# accumulator. The DDM has a single rate, its drift, which is the balance of
# the evidence for the two responses: turned towards the correct response
# (tidy_all_models()), it goes in the row of the rate towards correct, and its
# variability in the row under it.
all_models_rows <- c(
  "rate correct" = "Evidence rate\ntowards correct", "rate error" = "Evidence rate\ntowards error",
  "ratevar correct" = "Rate variability\ntowards correct", "ratevar error" = "Rate variability\ntowards error",
  "boundary correct" = "Boundary", "start correct" = "Starting\npoint",
  "startrange correct" = "Start-point\nrange", "ndt correct" = "Non-decision\ntime"
)
error_parameters <- c("nuone", "driftone", "sigmaone")

# The heatmaps of every model of one illusion, with the row of each parameter
tidy_all_models <- function(preds) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(preds[intersect(paper_models, names(preds))], \(p, model) {
    map <- family_components[[p$meta$family]]
    ddm <- p$meta$family == "cogmod_ddm"
    p$heatmaps |>
      filter(Parameter %in% names(map)) |>
      restore_units(illusion = p$meta$illusion) |>
      mutate(Model = model,
             Row = paste(map[Parameter], ifelse(Parameter %in% error_parameters, "error", "correct")),
             Predicted = case_when(ddm & Parameter == "mu" ~ -Predicted,
                                   ddm & Parameter == "bias" ~ 1 - Predicted,
                                   .default = Predicted))
  }) |>
    mutate(Row = factor(all_models_rows[Row], levels = all_models_rows))
}

# Axis breaks strictly inside the range, so that the labels of neighbouring
# panels do not run into each other
inner_breaks <- function(n) {
  \(limits) {
    b <- scales::breaks_extended(n)(limits)
    b[b > limits[1] + 0.02 * diff(limits) & b < limits[2] - 0.02 * diff(limits)]
  }
}

# One column per model, on its colour, and one row per process, in its colour.
# The parameters are on scales that cannot be compared, between models or
# within one, so every panel has its own colour scale, from its lowest value
# to its highest, and says what these are. What reads off the colours is the
# shape of an effect: which way it runs and where it bends. Its size is in the
# numbers. The contour lines mark every sixth of the panel's range.
#
# `palette` is the colours of that scale, from the lowest value to the highest.
# Spectral, from blue through yellow to red (user's choice, 2026-11-24, out of
# eight tried): it has more hues along it than viridis, and so shows more of
# the relief, without the neon green and cyan of turbo, which the heatmaps
# above use. Its pale yellow is only the middle of a panel's range, not a
# reference value.
plot_all_models <- function(preds, illusion = "MullerLyer",
                            palette = grDevices::hcl.colors(256, "Spectral", rev = TRUE)) {
  d <- tidy_all_models(preds[[illusion]]) |>
    mutate(.by = c(Model, Row), Scaled = scales::rescale(Predicted))
  shown <- intersect(paper_models, unique(d$Model))
  d$Model <- factor(d$Model, levels = shown)
  row_colours <- component_colours[sub(" .*", "", names(all_models_rows))]

  # Two significant digits, and a plain 0 for what rounds to it (a rate of 7e-8)
  short <- \(x) {
    if (abs(x) < 0.005) return("0")
    sub("^-", "−", format(signif(x, 2), drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE))
  }
  ranges <- d |>
    summarise(.by = c(Model, Row),
              Label = paste(short(min(Predicted)), "to", short(max(Predicted))),
              x = mean(range(Illusion_Strength)), y = max(Illusion_Difference))
  border <- if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "4.0.0") list(linewidth = 0) else list(label.size = 0)

  # A process that a model does not estimate is a grey cell, the grey of the
  # fixed parameters in the models figure, so that the grid reads as a table
  # with holes in it and not as a scatter of panels
  absent <- tidyr::expand_grid(Model = factor(shown, levels = shown),
                               Row = factor(levels(d$Row), levels = levels(d$Row))) |>
    anti_join(distinct(d, Model, Row), by = c("Model", "Row")) |>
    mutate(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf)

  ggplot(d, aes(Illusion_Strength, Illusion_Difference)) +
    geom_raster(aes(fill = Scaled)) +
    geom_contour(aes(z = Scaled), breaks = (1:5) / 6, colour = "white", alpha = 0.45, linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    # After the line at no illusion, which would otherwise cross the grey cells
    geom_rect(data = absent, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#ECECEC") +
    do.call(geom_label, c(list(data = ranges, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, label = Label), vjust = 1.15,
                               size = 1.75, fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8),
                               label.padding = grid::unit(1, "pt")), border)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = palette, breaks = c(0, 1), labels = c("lowest", "highest"),
                         guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "left", barwidth = grid::unit(6, "lines"),
                                                 barheight = grid::unit(0.5, "lines"))) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = inner_breaks(4)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = inner_breaks(4)) +
    ggh4x::facet_grid2(
      Row ~ Model, switch = "y",
      strip = ggh4x::strip_themed(
        background_x = ggh4x::elem_list_rect(fill = model_colors[shown],
                                             colour = rep("white", length(shown))),
        text_x = ggh4x::elem_list_text(colour = rep("white", length(shown)),
                                       face = rep("bold", length(shown))),
        text_y = ggh4x::elem_list_text(colour = row_colours, face = rep("bold", length(row_colours)))
      )
    ) +
    labs(x = "Illusion strength (negative: congruent, positive: incongruent)",
         y = "Objective difference between the targets (larger is easier)",
         fill = "Value, within each panel ") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 7, lineheight = 0.9),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing = grid::unit(4, "pt"),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 5),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7.5, vjust = 0.9),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.margin = margin(t = -4))
}
```

## Appendix: stanli Against cmdstanr

Three models were fitted with both samplers on the Muller-Lyer: LNR (stanli
0.21.0), and RDM-5 and DDM-4 (stanli 0.22.2) (`server/AGENT.md` 6.6-6.9). Only
the sampler differs: the same Stan program, data, priors, inits, shards, chains
and threads. Two samplers of one posterior should agree on everything but speed,
to within Monte Carlo error. A larger difference means that one of them missed
part of the posterior. Convergence then says which one to trust, not the
sampler.

```{r}
# Both fits of every model that has a stanli one (`twins`, from the loading
# chunk). A cmdstanr fit that is not there yet is NULL.
twin_preds <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(twins)), \(i) list(
  cmdstanr = if (twins$cmdstanr[i]) load_predictions(twins$Name[i], "cmdstanr"),
  stanli = load_predictions(twins$Name[i], "stanli")
))
twins$Label <- paste0(twins$Model, " (", twins$Illusion, ")")
names(twin_preds) <- twins$Label
complete <- twins$cmdstanr

# One row per fit, the two fits of a model one above the other. The ELPD
# difference is stanli's minus cmdstanr's, with the SE that loo_compare() would
# give it: both fits are of the same trials, so the pointwise values pair up
# (`yhash`, loo's hash of the outcome, checks that they do). The Monte Carlo
# SE is that of the difference, from every trial's own MCSE, and is the yardstick:
# a difference within about twice it is what two runs of one sampler would give.
# loo's mcse_loo() returns NA as soon as one trial has a Pareto k above 0.7,
# which every fit here has, and those trials' MCSEs are underestimated, so read
# it as a lower bound.
table_sampler_agreement <- function(twin_preds) {
  rows <- purrr::imap_dfr(twin_preds, \(pair, label) {
    loo_c <- pair$cmdstanr$loo
    loo_s <- pair$stanli$loo
    if (!identical(attr(loo_c, "yhash"), attr(loo_s, "yhash"))) {
      stop(label, ": the two fits are not of the same trials.")
    }
    d <- loo_s$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"] - loo_c$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"]
    mcse <- sqrt(sum(loo_c$pointwise[, "mcse_elpd_loo"]^2, loo_s$pointwise[, "mcse_elpd_loo"]^2))
    purrr::imap_dfr(pair, \(p, sampler) {
      conv <- p$convergence
      data.frame(
        Model = label,
        Family = sub(" .*", "", label),
        Sampler = sampler,
        ELPD = sprintf("%s ± %s", formatC(p$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", 1], format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
                       formatC(p$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", 2], format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")),
        p_loo = formatC(p$loo$estimates["p_loo", 1], format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
        "ELPD diff ± SE" = if (sampler == "stanli") sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f", sum(d), sqrt(length(d)) * sd(d)) else "",
        "Monte Carlo SE" = if (sampler == "stanli") sprintf("%.1f", mcse) else "",
        "R-hat, population (max)" = formatC(conv$rhat_pop_max, format = "f", digits = 3),
        "R-hat, lp__" = formatC(conv$rhat_lp, format = "f", digits = 3),
        # Chains in different modes show here first: within a mode the chain
        # means of lp__ sit within a few tens of each other (sd ~110)
        "lp__, spread of the chain means" = formatC(diff(range(conv$lp_chain_mean)), format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","),
        check.names = FALSE
      )
    })
  })
  tinytable::tt(select(rows, -Family)) |>
    tinytable::style_tt(j = 3:9, align = "r") |>
    fill_cells(1, model_fill(rows$Family))
}

plot_sampler_curves <- function(pair, label) {
  # The mean RT stands for the RT (the median has no SE to measure the gap
  # in), and the 5 difficulty levels every file has (coarse_levels()). The Z
  # difference is rounded so that the same level from a 5-level and a 9-level
  # file pairs up.
  curves <- purrr::imap_dfr(pair, \(p, sampler) mutate(p$curves, Sampler = sampler)) |>
    restore_units(illusion = pair$stanli$meta$illusion) |>
    filter(Parameter != "Median RT") |>
    mutate(Illusion_Difference = round(Illusion_Difference, 5),
           Illusion_DifferenceZ = round(Illusion_DifferenceZ, 6)) |>
    filter(Illusion_Difference %in% coarse_levels(Illusion_Difference))

  gap <- curves |>
    select(Parameter, Type, Illusion_StrengthZ, Illusion_DifferenceZ, Sampler, Predicted, SE) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Sampler, values_from = c(Predicted, SE)) |>
    summarise(.by = Parameter,
              Gap = max(abs(Predicted_stanli - Predicted_cmdstanr) / SE_cmdstanr, na.rm = TRUE))
  curves <- curves |>
    left_join(gap, by = "Parameter") |>
    mutate(Panel = sprintf("%s (gap %.2f SD)", Parameter, Gap),
           Illusion_Difference = factor(round(Illusion_Difference, 5)))

  curve_cols <- colorRampPalette(
    c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50")
  )(nlevels(curves$Illusion_Difference))

  ggplot(curves, aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted, colour = Illusion_Difference,
                     group = interaction(Sampler, Illusion_Difference))) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = Sampler), linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~Panel, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = curve_cols) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("cmdstanr" = "solid", "stanli" = "dashed")) +
    labs(title = label, x = "Illusion Strength", y = NULL, colour = "Task Difficulty") +
    theme_minimal()
}

table_sampler_speed <- function(twin_preds) {
  rows <- purrr::imap_dfr(twin_preds, \(pair, label) {
    time_c <- median(pair$cmdstanr$efficiency$Time_total)
    purrr::imap_dfr(pair, \(p, sampler) {
      e <- p$efficiency
      data.frame(
        Model = label,
        Family = sub(" .*", "", label),
        Sampler = sampler,
        Chains = nrow(e),
        "Step size (median)" = formatC(median(p$convergence$stepsize_chain), format = "f", digits = 4),
        "Warmup (h)" = sprintf("%.0f", median(e$Time_warmup) / 3600),
        "Sampling (h)" = sprintf("%.0f", median(e$Time_sample) / 3600),
        "Total (h)" = sprintf("%.0f", median(e$Time_total) / 3600),
        "Against cmdstanr" = sprintf("%.2fx", median(e$Time_total) / time_c),
        "Bulk ESS / h" = sprintf("%.1f", mean(e$ESS_per_hour)),
        check.names = FALSE
      )
    })
  })
  tinytable::tt(select(rows, -Family)) |>
    tinytable::style_tt(j = 3:9, align = "r") |>
    fill_cells(1, model_fill(rows$Family)) |>
    tinytable::group_tt(j = list("Per chain, median" = 4:7))
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Agreement

The ELPD difference is stanli's minus cmdstanr's. A difference within about
twice the Monte Carlo SE is what two runs of one sampler would give. Chains in
different modes show first in the spread of the chain means of `lp__`.

```{r}
if (any(complete)) {
  table_sampler_agreement(twin_preds[complete])
} else {
  cat("No model has both fits yet.\n")
}
```

### Parameter Curves

The predicted curves of each parameter along illusion strength, with cmdstanr
solid and stanli dashed. Each panel gives the largest gap between the two over
the grid, in posterior SDs of the cmdstanr fit.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| warning: false

# warning: false for the Mean RT, which is NA at the grid points where a fit
# predicts no response of that kind, and ggplot says so
if (any(complete)) {
  for (label in names(twin_preds)[complete]) print(plot_sampler_curves(twin_preds[[label]], label))
} else {
  cat("No model has both fits yet.\n")
}
```

### Speed

Wall clock per chain. Both fits ran on the same three nodes, which are shared
with other users and do not run at the same speed, and neither fit records
which node each chain ran on. So read a gap of a few tens of percent with
caution: `server/AGENT.md` 6.6-6.8 compares the two samplers node by node.

```{r}
if (any(complete)) {
  table_sampler_speed(twin_preds[complete])
} else {
  cat("No model has both fits yet.\n")
}
```

:::
